name: Create a model
description: A competitor naming a model. AN ENTRY IS A NAME: unique per owner per game, and addressed by its id ever after. It used to be a GitHub repository, normalised by repo_path() and confirmed against `GET /repos/{owner}/{name}` before the insert -- and that requirement limited nothing. Every ceiling on a competitor is a season rule (entries.max_per_user, max_per_class, in_flight_max, versions_max_per_*, cooldown_s, unique_weights) and not one of them mentioned a repository, while the check cost a SQL normaliser, a season predicate, two unique indexes and an outbound call on the create path THAT FAILED CLOSED -- so a rate-limited GitHub meant nobody could create an entry at all. GitHub is now the sign-in identity and nothing else, and this route reaches no host outside the deployment. Write, then diagnose: the insert carries every remaining rule as a predicate so a refusal is a row that was never written, and `why` reads back which one it was, through the same functions. A model is created empty; POST /v1/submissions is what puts a version under it.

body.detail: name is what you call this model. It has to be unique among your own entries for this game.

tasks.name: Find the game
tasks.description: A game that does not exist is a 404 before any rule is asked. It used to also normalise the repository here, ahead of the call to GitHub; there is no call and no repository now, so the read is the game alone.

input.query: SELECT g.id::text AS game_id FROM games g WHERE g.slug = ($1)::text

INSERT INTO models (owner_id, game_id, name) SELECT ($1)::uuid, g.id, btrim(($3)::text) FROM games g JOIN live_sessions ls ON ls.sid = ($4)::uuid AND ls.user_id = ($1)::uuid LEFT JOIN seasons s ON s.game_id = g.id AND s.closed_at IS NULL WHERE g.slug = ($2)::text AND btrim(($3)::text) <> '' AND length(btrim(($3)::text)) <= 64 AND (s.id IS NULL OR season_admits(s, ($1)::uuid)) AND (s.id IS NULL OR season_admits_entry(s, ($1)::uuid)) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM models e WHERE e.owner_id = ($1)::uuid AND e.game_id = g.id AND lower(e.name) = lower(btrim(($3)::text)))

SELECT json_build_object( 'name', btrim(($3)::text), 'participant', s.id IS NULL OR season_admits(s, ($2)::uuid), 'room', s.id IS NULL OR season_admits_entry(s, ($2)::uuid), 'entries_max', (s.rules -> 'entries' ->> 'max_per_user')::int, 'entries_used', (SELECT count(*) FROM models e WHERE e.owner_id = ($2)::uuid AND e.game_id = g.id AND e.retired_at IS NULL), 'name_taken', EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM models e WHERE e.owner_id = ($2)::uuid AND e.game_id = g.id AND lower(e.name) = lower(btrim(($3)::text)))) AS body FROM games g LEFT JOIN seasons s ON s.game_id = g.id AND s.closed_at IS NULL WHERE g.slug = ($1)::text

tasks.name: Read the entry back
tasks.description: Keyed on the name, which models_owner_game_name_uniq makes a key: db_write answers only rows_affected, so the created row is read back, and the read-back needs a unique predicate. It used to be the repository.

input.query: SELECT json_build_object('model_id', e.id, 'model', e.name, 'game', g.slug, 'owner', u.handle, 'created_at', e.created_at, 'versions', '[]'::json) AS body FROM models e JOIN games g ON g.id = e.game_id JOIN users u ON u.id = e.owner_id JOIN live_sessions s ON s.sid = ($4)::uuid AND s.user_id = e.owner_id WHERE e.owner_id = ($1)::uuid AND g.slug = ($2)::text AND lower(e.name) = lower(btrim(($3)::text))
